findings.summary: The "Tidy Blind Spot" sidebox inverts `go mod tidy`'s actual build-tag behaviour: tidy enables *all* build tags, with `ignore` the only exception.
findings.evidence: "Excluded files are invisible to `go mod tidy`'s scan" / "Their imports can vanish from `go.mod`" / "Tidy covers all GOOS/GOARCH but NOT custom tags" — but the Go Modules Reference states "As with `go mod tidy` and other module commands, build constraints except for `ignore` are not considered", and `go help mod tidy` says "Tidy acts as if all build tags are enabled, so it will consider platform-specific source files and files that require custom build tags ... There is one exception: the \"ignore\" build tag is not enabled." This also contradicts page 4's own "Pin tools in `tools.go` behind `//go:build tools` / Then tidy keeps their versions pinned for you", which only works because custom tags ARE scanned.
findings.fix: Replace the box with the correct rule: "Tidy ignores build constraints entirely — all GOOS/GOARCH *and* custom tags are scanned, so `tools.go` behind `//go:build tools` keeps tool deps in `go.mod`. The one exception is `//go:build ignore`: those files are invisible to tidy, so imports only used there will be dropped."

findings.summary: The caption's first sentence is a series label rather than a hook, burying the actual hook in sentence two where the feed truncates.
findings.evidence: "Part 2 of GO MODULES. Every Go build you ship is decided by two text files and one algorithm that picks the LOWEST version that works — the opposite of npm."
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and demote the label: "Every Go build you ship is decided by two text files and one algorithm that picks the LOWEST version that works — the opposite of npm. (Part 2 of GO MODULES.)"

findings.summary: The vendoring page explains when vendor mode activates before it ever says what vendoring is or what `go mod vendor` produces, so `modules.txt` is used as a trigger condition before it is defined.
findings.evidence: The page opens with heading "When It Turns On" and the table row ["`modules.txt` + go 1.14+","`-mod=vendor` by default"]; only afterwards does "What Gets Copied" state "`vendor/modules.txt` records paths, versions, go lines", and the command `go mod vendor` first appears in the code block near the bottom of the page.
findings.fix: Move a one-block definition to the top of page 1 — "`go mod vendor` copies every package needed to build and test the main module into `./vendor`, and writes `vendor/modules.txt`" — then keep "When It Turns On" as the second section.
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: The closing tip on the constraint-syntax page instructs learners to split code by filename suffix, a mechanism not introduced until the next page.
findings.evidence: Page 2 callout: "Split per-platform code into `x_linux.go` and `x_windows.go` with the **same** function names — no `runtime.GOOS` branching at run time." The rule that filenames are constraints appears only on page 3: "Filename-based constraints" table with "`file_linux.go` — GOOS=linux".
findings.fix: Either move the "Two Files, One API" callout to page 3 after the "Filename Constraints" table, or add one line to it stating that a `_linux`/`_windows` filename suffix is itself an implicit build constraint (covered next page).

findings.summary: Wrong version for the removal of `go get`'s install behaviour — it was Go 1.18, not Go 1.22.
findings.evidence: "Since Go 1.22 `go get` no longer installs binaries" — the Go 1.18 release notes: "`go get` no longer builds or installs packages in module-aware mode. `go get` is now dedicated to adjusting dependencies in `go.mod`. Effectively the `-d` flag is always enabled." (Go 1.22's `go get` change was only about dropping support outside a module in GOPATH mode.)
findings.fix: Change to "Since Go 1.18 `go get` no longer installs binaries (deprecated in 1.16)".

findings.summary: The caption's page count does not match the deck.
findings.evidence: Caption: "Ten pages on go.mod internals, pseudo-versions, semantic import versioning, MVS, the checksum database, replace/retract, vendoring and build tags." — this part contains 8 slides, and pseudo-versions, semantic import versioning, MVS and the checksum database are not covered on any of them.
findings.fix: State the real count for this part (eight pages) and list only its topics, or make it explicit that the sentence describes the whole handbook across both parts.

findings.summary: Claims vendoring breaks dependencies that rely on embedded files, but `go mod vendor` has resolved and copied `//go:embed` patterns since Go 1.17.
findings.evidence: "Breaks deps relying on embedded testdata or generated files" — `cmd/go/internal/modcmd/vendor.go` calls `load.ResolveEmbed(bp.Dir, embedPatterns)` and copies the matched files into `vendor/` (golang/go#43077).
findings.fix: Narrow the bullet to what actually breaks: "Files a dep opens at run time (non-`//go:embed` assets, testdata) are dropped; `//go:embed` patterns are resolved and copied."

findings.summary: The pinned annotation box is anchored on top of the code block so its pin graphic collides with the end of the code line.
findings.evidence: The sticky note "blank line below the tag is mandatory" sits inside the //go:build code block, with its red pin drawn over the tail of "package fsx // pure-Go path".
findings.fix: Offset the annotation anchor down/right (as on slide 6, where the pin sits in empty block space) so the pin never lands on a code glyph.

findings.summary: The grammar table uses the implicit tags `unix`, `cgo`, and the `js` GOOS as if known, but the list of always-available tags is only given on page 3.
findings.evidence: Page 2 table row ["`(unix || js) && !cgo`","grouped + negated"]; page 3 later says "Tags You Get Free — GOOS, GOARCH, `cgo`, `gc` / `gccgo`, `unix` (1.19+)".
findings.fix: Use only GOOS/GOARCH names already shown (e.g. `(linux || darwin) && !windows`) in the page 2 grammar table, and keep the `unix`/`cgo` example on page 3 where those tags are defined.

findings.summary: Off-by-one version boundary for dropping `// +build` lines — `//go:build` alone is understood from Go 1.17, not 1.18.
findings.evidence: "1.17+ writes both forms; 1.18+ needs only the new one" — Go 1.17 introduced `//go:build` and builds files that carry only that line; `gofmt` adds `// +build` only to keep pre-1.17 toolchains working.
findings.fix: Change to "1.17 understands the new form; drop `// +build` once your minimum toolchain is 1.17+".

findings.summary: The "Tidy Blind Spot" sidebox prescribes a `tools.go` fix and relies on `go mod tidy`'s pruning behavior before either is explained on page 4.
findings.evidence: Page 3 sidebox: "Their imports can vanish from `go.mod` ... Fix: a `tools.go` with a tag plus explicit imports." Page 4 is where tidy is defined ("`go mod tidy` adds every missing require, drops every unused one") and where the `tools.go` example is shown ("//go:build tools ... import _ \"a.com/cmd/lint\"").
findings.fix: Replace the bare "Fix:" line with a forward pointer ("Fix: a tagged `tools.go` — see the next page"), or move the sidebox to page 4 directly above the existing `tools.go` code block.

findings.summary: The legacy `// +build` syntax is presented at the top of the filename-suffix page instead of next to the modern syntax it contrasts with, splitting one topic across two pages in reverse order.
findings.evidence: Page 3's first block is the sidebox "Legacy Form" — "`// +build linux,amd64` — comma = AND", "1.17+ writes both forms; 1.18+ needs only the new one" — while page 2, titled "Build Constraint Syntax & Grammar", presents only `//go:build` and its grammar.
findings.fix: Move the "Legacy Form" sidebox onto page 2 beside the `//go:build` grammar table, so both syntaxes and the `gofmt` sync rule are taught together before filenames are introduced.

findings.summary: `go mod verify` is described as checking the cache against `go.sum`, but it checks against the hash recorded in the module cache at download time.
findings.evidence: "`go mod verify` re-hashes the cache against `go.sum`" — the reference says it "hashes each downloaded module .zip file and extracted directory, then compares those hashes with a hash recorded when the module was first downloaded", and `verify.go` reads `zip+"hash"` (the cache's `.ziphash` file); it never reads `go.sum`. go.sum is checked on download, not by `go mod verify`.
findings.fix: Reword to "`go mod verify` re-hashes the cache against the hashes recorded at download time — it detects a tampered cache, not a bad `go.sum`".

findings.summary: The CI checklist orders readers to pin the CI Go version with no reason given; the justification appears two pages later.
findings.evidence: Page 5: "Pin the CI Go version to match the `go` line" (no supporting explanation). Page 7: "A newer `go` line makes old toolchains refuse to build" / "Match the CI image to the `go` line".
findings.fix: Move the "Toolchain Mismatch" sidebox from page 7 onto page 5 next to the checklist item, so the rule and its cause are read together.
